Additionally, we investigate the implications of a morphism being recognizable in a subshift and prove that this recognition leads to a bijective measure transfer function under certain conditions. A key component of our proof is a proposition that characterizes a recognizable morphism based on its injective mapping properties and its ability to preserve the periodicity of certain words within a subshift.

Building on the general framework of perturbative quantum field theory for the pure Yang-Mills model, we demonstrate that tree-level contributions are anomaly-free, and we will derive a more comprehensive expression of this gauge invariance property.

A package manager plays a vital role in technology stacks by facilitating the
installation, configuration, or removal of verified dependency packages within
an application. As various technology stacks have led to multiple package
managers with distinct features, our research sought to uncover issues faced by
end-users. An empirical study analyzing Stack Overflow content for three
popular package managers, namely Maven, npm, and NuGet, revealed the
challenges users encounter while using these tools. Our findings show that a
substantial proportion of end-users (approximately 64-72%) experience issues
with PM tool usage. The root causes of these problems include insufficient
instructions and unclear error messages from the package managers. We also
found that users frequently resolve these issues by sharing links to external
resources, such as official documentation and tutorials, indicating the need
for better tool support and more relevant information for end-users.

A one-dimensional torus associated with a separable commutative algebra over a global field is classified as a Kummer type if each component of the algebra is a cyclic extension of the form associated with a Kummer theory. This paper applies existing theories by Bayer-Fluckiger, T-Y. Lee and Parimala and by T-Y. Lee to calculate the Tate-Shafarevich group for tori of this type. Furthermore, we have developed a computational algorithm, implemented using the SAGE software, to calculate the Tate-Shafarevich groups in the case where each component of the algebra is contained within a fixed concrete bicomposite extension of the base field.

New breakthroughs in biological technologies, exemplified by multi-way chromosome
conformation capture (3C), necessitate the creation of tools for dissecting complex interactions.
Hypergraphs offer a mathematical framework for accurately modeling and dissecting multi-way interactions.
In this context, we introduce the Hypergraph Analysis Toolbox (HAT), a software tool designed for 
interpreting and visualizing multi-way interactions in intricate biological systems.
For any two minimal models of a generalized lc pair, there are smaller birational models connected by a sequence of flip operations.

To reduce the impact of outliers, a multi-neighbourhood kNN ensemble employs majority voting to estimate a new data point's classification by selecting a set of closest neighbours from a neighbourhood. Standard kNN techniques, however, rely on a distance formula to determine k neighbours enclosed within a spherical region, which may not work when test data follow a curved pattern outside the sphere. Moreover, combining hundreds of individual kNN models with potential high error rates can lead to suboptimal ensembles. Therefore, an improved extended neighbourhood rule ensemble is introduced, where k nearest neighbours are identified in stages by successively selecting the closest points to previously chosen ones. Each ensemble model is built using a random subset of features and a bootstrap sample, and the optimal models are selected based on their performance on unseen out-of-bag data.

Deep learning models for analyzing point process data, prevalent in social media, healthcare, and finance, often fall short in capturing complex time-varying patterns due to their inherent structures. However, a promising alternative involves modeling point processes by decomposing their influence kernels using neural networks. Our research adopts this approach, introducing a novel deep model capable of handling non-stationary spatial and temporal point processes. This model employs a low-rank decomposition technique to efficiently represent complex point processes, ensuring faster computations and superior results. To enforce the non-negativity constraint of conditional intensities, we propose a log-barrier penalty method. Our proposed method demonstrates superior performance and efficiency over existing techniques on simulated and real-world datasets.

This paper introduces an end-to-end neural mapping approach for camera positioning that represents an entire scene through a grid of latent codes, which a Transformer-based decoder uses to estimate 3D coordinates for specific pixels. In contrast to current best practices in camera localization, which store scenes as 3D point clouds with associated features, taking up considerable storage space, NeuMap achieves remarkable compression rates without significant performance loss. By employing 1) trainable latent codes to store scene data and 2) a Transformer-based auto-decoder applicable to any scene, NeuMap significantly reduces the storage requirements for scenes. Furthermore, the scene-agnostic network learns robust matching patterns using large datasets and enables the rapid optimization of scene codes without retraining the network. Comprehensive evaluations across five benchmarks reveal NeuMap outperforms other coordinate regression methods and matches the performance of feature matching methods while utilizing a significantly smaller scene representation. Specifically, NeuMap achieves 39.1% accuracy in the Aachen night benchmark using merely 6MB of data, whereas competing methods necessitate 100MB or several gigabytes and struggle under high compression settings.

From two distinct perspectives, regret minimization and competitive analysis, we examine the core challenge of real-time control of a linear system. Our findings demonstrate that the optimal policy for competitive analysis can be closely approximated by a specific policy class, known as disturbance-action control policies, which can be parameterized convexly. Utilizing this key insight, we reveal that several online control algorithms have achieved a remarkable balance between regret and competitive performance. Specifically, these algorithms can obtain sublinear regret in comparison to the optimal DAC policy selected post facto and the optimal competitive ratio, with the only exception being a sublinearly growing correction factor in the time horizon. Furthermore, we establish that sublinear regret with respect to the optimal competitive policy is feasible even when the linear system's dynamics are unknown or a pre-existing stabilizing controller is unavailable.

Discovering effective update rules for black-box optimization techniques like evolution strategies without access to gradients is a key challenge, one that can be overcome by applying the principles of meta-learning. Our research focuses on addressing the heuristic and inflexible nature of evolution strategies through meta-learning, and we achieve this by designing a search strategy based on self-attention architecture, ensuring the learned update rules are invariant to the order of candidate solutions. Through meta-learning on a small set of low-dimensional optimization problems, we successfully develop a new evolution strategy that can generalize to various unseen optimization problems, population sizes, and time horizons. Additionally, we demonstrate the competitive performance of this strategy on both supervised and continuous control tasks. Furthermore, our approach allows for the evaluation of individual components of the method, the conversion of the learned strategy into a clear heuristic form, and the possibility of self-referential training of an evolution strategy using the learned update rule to drive the outer meta-learning loop.

Traditional text-to-SQL research has been constrained to single tasks with static training and testing sets. However, in real-world scenarios where numerous tasks are encountered, existing methods face significant challenges due to inadequate supervised data and high retraining costs. This leads to two major issues: the model overfits to new task databases due to a lack of supervised data, and it forgets previously learned SQL structures and database schemas due to limited retraining. To address these issues, this paper proposes integrating semi-supervised learning and continual learning into a stream of text-to-SQL tasks and presents two novel solutions. The initial solution, 'Vanilla,' employs self-training to generate pseudo-labeled instances based on predicted labels, while using episodic memory replay to balance efficiency with performance on past tasks. The improved 'SFNet' solution leverages the connection between CL and SSL by utilizing in-memory past information to aid current SSL and enhancing future replay with high-quality pseudo instances. The experimental results demonstrate that SFNet outperforms widely used SSL-only and CL-only baselines on various metrics.

An examination of the Ground Wide Angle Camera's archive revealed a total of 43 stars emitting white light flares, out of which 3 were identified as homologous and one exhibited a periodic pulsation with a 13-minute cycle. Among the 43 flare stars, 19 were newly discovered, and 41 had light curves available from the TESS and/or K2 missions, resulting in the detection of 931 stellar flares. By analyzing these light curves, researchers determined the rotational or orbital periods for 34 flare stars, with 33 taking less than 5.4 days to complete. Furthermore, using low-resolution spectra from LAMOST and the Xinglong 2.16m telescope, the ratio of H-alpha emission to bolometric luminosity was found to be in a saturation state on the rotation-activity diagram. Observations of the medium-resolution spectrum of Star #3 (HAT 178-02667) revealed it to be a binary system, consisting of two active stars with dual H-alpha emissions. In addition, 13 of these stars had flare frequency distributions derived from their light curves, which showed that the detected GWAC flares occur between 0.5 to 9.5 times per year. Studies based on these flare frequency distributions indicated that the flares from some of these stars could potentially destroy the ozone layers of habitable planets, but none were found to trigger prebiotic chemistry on these planets.

Advanced multi-domain recommender systems typically cover various categories to cater to diverse user needs, with the aim of enhancing performance across all domains simultaneously. However, conventional methods using graph neural networks often treat each domain separately or share a model across all domains. This can result in either neglecting users' cross-domain behavior or failing to account for domain-specific preferences, thus limiting their performance in multi-domain recommendation. To overcome these limitations, it's crucial to leverage multi-domain user feedbacks and develop separate user representations that capture their domain-specific preferences. This paper presents $\mathsf{H^3Trans}$, a hierarchical framework that employs a hypergraph network to facilitate correlative preference transfer in multi-domain recommendation. By representing multiple domains within a unified graph, $\mathsf{H^3Trans}$ capitalizes on users' diverse behaviors to enable effective preference transfer. The proposed framework comprises two modules: the dynamic item transfer module, which extracts correlative information from multi-domain user feedbacks to eliminate item representation discrepancies, and the adaptive user aggregation module, which aggregates users' scattered preferences and exploits high-order connections to learn user representations. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of $\mathsf{H^3Trans}$ in multi-domain recommendation tasks on both public datasets and large-scale production datasets.

The inclusion of standard model Yukawa interactions in a grand unified theory frequently predicts multiple novel scalars which can couple to fermions and lead to observable consequences. In this context, we investigated the colour sextet diquark scalars within realistic renormalizable models based on $SO(10)$ grand unified theories, considering a spectrum of five sextets. After determining their explicit couplings to quarks, we analyzed their contributions to the mixing of neutral mesons and antimesons and to baryon number-violating processes such as neutron-antineutron oscillations. The latter arises due to a $B-L$ violating trilinear coupling between the sextets. We derived constraints on the sextet masses by considering the allowed values of the $B-L$ breaking scale and Yukawa couplings. The results suggest that certain sextets cannot be simultaneously lighter than the $B-L$ breaking scale, making their observation unlikely in near-future experiments. However, a possible scenario exists in which a sub-GUT scale $\Sigma$ and a pair of $S$, allowed by other constraints, could potentially produce the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe.

Mobile network operators are pushing for cost-efficient solutions with the development of 5G and beyond networks, necessitating highly adaptable deployments in dynamic and resource-scarce environments. In this context, we believe that zero-touch orchestration using cloud-native infrastructure with real-time monitoring capabilities can effectively address these challenges. This live demonstration, based on a comprehensive end-to-end 5G experimental platform featuring real-time transmissions, showcases how automated orchestration can efficiently relocate applications to meet specific intent-based demands. Furthermore, our experimental validation demonstrates the platform's ability to facilitate flexible and agile 5G deployments as desired.

The use of laser-generated bubbles under confinement as a driving force in microfluidic devices such as needle-free injectors has been researched. This study compares bubble formation produced by continuous and pulsed lasers within an open-ended microfluidic tube, providing insights into how different light emission patterns impact bubble dynamics. The study reveals that bubble growth accelerates linearly with energy input from both laser types, demonstrating their comparable effectiveness in creating liquid jets. However, it's noted that CW lasers require more energy due to heat dissipation and exhibit greater variability in bubble size and growth rates under consistent initial conditions.

The Gibbs partitions of integers generated by stable subordinators of index α∈(0,1) are significant classes of random partitions where substantial knowledge has been obtained about their properties, particularly with regards to complex asymptotic results that can be easily obtained. This class encompasses the well-known Poisson-Dirichlet distribution-based models that are predominantly utilized in applications. Building upon previous work, this study aims to provide interpretations for a broader class of Gibbs partitions by incorporating key operations within this framework. We address the challenge of expanding Jim Pitman's (1999, Annals of Probability) dual, infinite-block, coagulation/fragmentation results to encompass all Gibbs (stable Poisson-Kingman) models. Our findings yield nested families of Gibbs partitions and corresponding mass partitions over any 0<β<α<1, focusing on the fragmentation operations, which remain independent in this context. Additionally, we derive remarkable calculations for Gibbs partitions resulting from these operations. Furthermore, we provide definitive results for the dual coagulation operations, based on our construction of dependent processes, and illustrate its straightforward application in Mittag-Leffler and generalized gamma models, demonstrating an alternative method to recover Pitman's (1999) duality results.

This study introduces a feedback system design to ensure accurate and reliable epidemic surveillance by mitigating the impact of uncertain data and models. We employ historical epidemiological data to derive methods for estimating general epidemic model parameters, which may be influenced by noise in the data. To address parameter uncertainty and noisy measurements, an observer-based robust state estimation technique is proposed. Next, we develop optimal control policies by minimizing a cost functional based on the estimated model and state. The effectiveness of this method is verified through its application to a modified SIR epidemic model.

A key challenge in planning microbeam radiation therapy lies in quickly and accurately predicting treatment doses. To address this, our research proposes a machine learning model based on a 3D U-Net architecture. This model splits the dose prediction into two parts, estimating the intense doses from individual microbeams and the lower doses in between. By treating these dose components as larger, macroscopic quantities, we can more efficiently train the model. As a result, the model can automatically account for complex physical factors, such as polarization, by mirroring full Monte Carlo data. This approach enables us to create a detailed dose distribution that can be easily combined with other microbeam predictions, making it suitable for treatment planning. Our method can generate an entire microbeam irradiation field in under a minute while maintaining a reasonable level of accuracy.

Observations of the rapid radio brightening of GRB 210702A were made using the Australian Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) just 11 hours after the burst occurred. The observations tracked the early-time radio variability of the burst over a five-hour period on timescales of around 15 minutes at three different frequencies. A power-law fit of the light curve revealed that the burst peaked at a flux density of approximately 0.4 milliJansky 13 hours post-burst, with a steep rise and decline. The observed behavior is atypical of the standard internal-external shock model, which predicts longer timescales for radio emission from forward and reverse shocks. The early-time light curves in the optical and X-ray ranges, as observed by the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, demonstrated typical afterglow behavior and allowed us to determine a homogeneous circumburst medium and an emitting electron population power-law index. We propose that the early-time radio flare is likely due to the effect of weak interstellar scintillation, which temporarily boosted the radio afterglow emission to levels above the sensitivity limit of the ATCA. Using the relationships for weak ISS, we were able to constrain the upper limit on the size of the blast wave to be no larger than six times ten to the power of sixteen centimeters in the plane of the sky. This size is consistent with the theoretical forward shock size prediction for GRB 210702A at 13 hours post-burst, and it represents the earliest size constraint of its kind on a GRB blast wave. The findings highlight the importance of rapid radio follow-up of GRBs using multiple-hour integrations to capture the early afterglow evolution and track scintillation over a broad frequency range.

The research areas of multimodal sentiment analysis and emotion recognition in conversations are crucial for computers to comprehend human behavior. Emotions are transient expressions of affect, whereas sentiments represent more enduring attitudes. Most previous studies have addressed these topics independently and have failed to fully leverage the complementary insights they provide. This paper presents a novel framework called UniMSE that integrates sentiment analysis and emotion recognition by sharing knowledge across features, labels, and models. Our framework fuses modalities at both syntactic and semantic levels, employing contrastive learning techniques to capture the nuances between sentiments and emotions. Empirical evaluations on four benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques and provides consistent improvements.

A quantum neural network's ability to universally approximate any function is crucial to its effectiveness. Non-universal networks risk failing at machine learning tasks, but encoding data into tensor product copies is inefficient, leading to increased system size and complexity. To address this, we've developed a duplication-free quantum model, proven to be universal and requiring significantly fewer resources compared to existing proposals, while being more robust against noise and easier to implement on near-term devices. Our model has been shown to effectively solve a wide variety of problems, highlighting its potential applications.

This review provides an overview of research findings in mean-field coupled maps, beginning with foundational works from physics before moving on to more recent studies in ergodic theory that investigate globally coupled maps in the thermodynamic limit, including associated self-consistent transfer operators. Additionally, we touch upon related fields and applications of mean-field coupled systems, including those in continuous time.

Based on the authors' previous work, an S-adic development of a subshift X is linked to a series of directives, which comprise at each level n the measure cone and the letter frequency cone of its associated subshift X_n. This resulting framework allows researchers to deduce conclusions about X with clarity and simplicity. To illustrate, we identify a broad category of minimal subshifts with zero entropy that all possess an infinite number of ergodic probability measures. Additionally, as a byproduct, we demonstrate the existence of an S-adic development for any integer d greater than or equal to 2, representing a minimal, aperiodic, and uniquely ergodic subshift X, where the level alphabets all have a cardinality of d, yet none of the bottom level morphisms with d-2 elements can be recognized within its corresponding level subshift X_n in A_n^Z.

Developing molecules that specifically interact with target proteins is a difficult challenge in drug discovery research. Traditional methods of generating molecules often involve a sequential approach, generating atoms one by one based on their element type and 3D position, but this approach fails to capture the complex, interconnected relationships between atoms in real-world molecules, where the energy between atoms is interdependent. Consequently, this sequential method often disregards the fundamental physical laws governing molecular interactions, resulting in the generation of molecules with undesirable properties. In contrast, our proposed approach uses a non-sequential generative model, specifically a diffusion model, that can simultaneously learn the distribution of molecular structures and their properties given the context of a target protein. By leveraging this model, we are able to generate molecules that not only bind effectively to their target proteins but also exhibit favorable properties such as optimal size and chemical characteristics.

Health equity relies heavily on fairness in medical decision-making, but evaluating the fairness of such decisions using available data is difficult. Various fairness measures have been developed to quantify decision-making fairness, with a growing interest in causality-based fairness metrics due to their ability to account for biases and adjust for confounding factors. Despite their potential, causality-based fairness measures remain underutilized in clinical settings, particularly with large healthcare datasets. In this study, we introduce a Bayesian causal inference method to assess a specific causality-based fairness concept, principal fairness, in medical environments. Our approach is tested using both artificially generated data and real-world electronic health records.

Deep learning methods have demonstrated their value for sentiment analysis tasks.
Recurrent neural networks, particularly those with long short-term memory and
bidirectional architectures, serve as benchmarks for creating accurate predictive
models. Yet, these models' intricacy and numerous hyperparameters for tuning
give rise to questions about their reliability. This paper examines multiple LSTM
models and their core parameters, and it conducts experiments to assess their
stability within the context of sentiment analysis.

In this research, we explore the relationship between entanglement and global internal symmetries in de Sitter space. Focusing on two symmetrical areas separated by causality in the hyperbolic map of de Sitter space, we use entanglement measures to investigate the long-range correlations within the space. Given that certain theories exhibit additive global internal symmetry, we can break down entanglement measures into more precise, local charge sectors, offering a more detailed analysis. In this study, we consider two theories: a free complex scalar field and a free Dirac field on de Sitter space, both possessing global internal $U(1)$ symmetry. We calculate and examine the symmetry-resolved entanglement entropy of both theories in the Bunch-Davies vacuum state and discover that the entanglement entropy divides evenly among local charge sectors, up to negligible terms that decrease as the volume of the region increases, ultimately leading to an even division as the volume becomes infinitely large.

Instance segmentation is a widely used technique in image editing, analysis, and autonomous driving applications, but it's often hindered by a lack of sufficient training data. To address this challenge, the Visual Inductive Priors Instance Segmentation Challenge was created, focusing on finding effective solutions to work with limited data. In response to this problem, a novel Task-Specific Data Augmentation approach was developed to tackle the issue of data insufficiency, while also leveraging existing visual inductive priors through a complementary Task-Specific Inference Processing strategy. We applied our proposed method on the Hybrid Task Cascade based detector with a Swin-Base based CBNetV2 backbone to the 2022 VIPriors Instance Segmentation Challenge, achieving a competitive result of 0.531 AP@0.50:0.95 on the test set.

This paper presents an updated RATAN-600 catalogue featuring a large collection of blazars from various types, now exceeding 1700 entries with the addition of flat-spectrum radio quasars. The catalogue primarily comprises quasi-simultaneous radio continuum data for blazars measured at six frequencies by RATAN-600, supplemented with additional radio data from external sources to facilitate more comprehensive radio spectrum and light curve analyses. Furthermore, the catalogue offers tools for users to compute spectral indices, variability indices, and radio luminosities. The paper provides a concise overview of the catalogue's subsamples of blazar types, covering spectral classifications, spectral indices, flux density variability, and radio luminosities.

Utilizing data from electron-positron collisions gathered by the BESIII detector at the BEPCII storage rings, we've calculated the differential cross sections for the production of $\pi^0$ and $K^0_S$ mesons in relation to their momentum, relative to the total cross-section for hadron production in the $e^{+}e^{-} \to$ hadrons process, across six center-of-mass energy points ranging from 2.2324 to 3.6710 GeV. Our results covering 90% of the hadrons' energy distribution show significant discrepancies with theoretical predictions based on current fragmentation functions, particularly at lower energies.

Person re-identification has made significant strides, particularly in recent years. A growing focus is now on long-term identification involving changes of clothing. Current methods primarily concentrate on image-based scenarios, overlooking crucial temporal data. This paper explores the understudied area of person re-identification from video data with clothes-changing occurrences, addressing both the challenge of inconsistent attire and temporal information in videos. To tackle this, a two-branch re-ranking framework is developed, which utilizes appearance features and gait features free from clothing changes, guided by a confidence-based ranking strategy. This method establishes a foundation for future research. Furthermore, two new benchmark datasets have been created, comprising a synthetic and a real-world dataset featuring individuals with diverse clothing changes, to facilitate comparative analysis and future studies.

Research into cold and controlled molecular ions plays a vital role in the advancement of physics and chemistry. Studies focusing on the cooling of molecular anions have led to groundbreaking discoveries, particularly in the production of cold antihydrogen, anionic Coulomb crystals, atmospheric studies, and astrochemistry. However, conventional anion cooling methods through collisions with a buffer gas have limitations due to the temperature constraints of cryogenic cooling mediums. Our research presents a novel technique of forced evaporative cooling of anions via a laser beam, where photons have energies significantly higher than the photodetachment threshold of the anion. This innovative method enabled the successful evaporative cooling of an OH$^{-}$ ensemble from an initial temperature of 370(12) K down to 2.2(8) K. Our findings demonstrate a substantial three orders of magnitude increase in the ions' phase space density, pushing the boundaries of Coulomb coupling regime. A detailed thermodynamic model, accounting for intrinsic collisional heating, was employed to quantify the anion cooling dynamics without any adjustable parameters. This technique holds the potential to cool any anionic species below liquid helium temperatures, opening new avenues for anion cooling and expanding the current understanding of anion physics.

The significance of non-potential magnetic energy in identifying the trigger for solar coronal eruptions remains unclear. To investigate this, we performed three-dimensional MHD simulations of a system prone to coronal jets, comparing the magnetic energy and helicity dynamics under different driving conditions. Two simulations shared the same setup and forcing profile, but one had prolonged driving, resulting in an induced helical jet with significant delay. The system without jet production had shorter driving, which also produced a lower value of non-potential energy and helicity. Analyzing the phase following the driving phase, magnetic energy remained stable while magnetic helicities showed a significant change. During this post-driving phase, the ratio of non-potential energy to total energy decreased slightly, and a helicity index increased. The jet generation occurred when the system reached its highest helicity index value, which subsequently decreased during jet production. The free energy also decreased but did not peak during jet generation.

We investigate the magnetic phase diagram of a collection of dipolar hard spheres (DHS), either with or without uniaxial anisotropy, immobilized in a random arrangement via tempered Monte Carlo simulations. A pivotal aspect is examining an anisotropic arrangement obtained by quenching the DHS fluid from the liquid state into a polarized state at low temperatures. The glass transition temperature, $\beta_f$, influences the structure's degree of anisotropy, measured through a structural nematic order parameter, $\lambda_s$. We consider only the infinitely strong uniaxial anisotropy case, resulting in a dipolar Ising model (DIM). A significant finding is that both DHS with and without a frozen structure, and DIM, exhibit a ferromagnetic phase at volume fractions below the threshold value, in contrast to isotropic DHS systems, which show a spin glass phase at low temperatures.

Our research demonstrates that a particular subset of flag varieties of a Kac-Moody group, specifically the totally nonnegative part of their twisted product, can be divided into distinct, manageable components, each of whose boundaries is a complex geometric shape resembling a closed sphere. This finding has several key implications. Firstly, the space of totally nonnegative braids, a related concept, also consists of these same manageable components arranged in a complex geometric pattern. Secondly, our work resolves an outstanding question in the field by showing that the boundary regions surrounding individual "double Bruhat cells" in a broader geometric context are also geometric shapes resembling a closed sphere.

The field of generative models has seen considerable advancements thanks to access to vast datasets and pre-trained models. Nevertheless, the majority of symbolic music datasets are extremely limited, which hinders the performance of data-driven models that incorporate multiple formats. To address this issue, one potential strategy is to utilize pre-trained models from other modalities (such as natural language) to enhance the performance of tasks involving symbolic music and multiple formats. In this research, we conducted the initial study of generating comprehensive and semantically coherent symbolic music scores from text descriptions, and evaluated the effectiveness of leveraging publicly available models for natural language processing in text-to-music generation. Our experiments demonstrated that utilizing pre-trained models led to a statistically significant improvement in terms of BLEU score and edit distance similarity. Furthermore, we investigated the capabilities and limitations of our model to better understand the potential of language-music models.

We conducted a search for the tree-diagram dominated process $B^+ \rightarrow p \overline{n} \pi^0$ using a large dataset of $772 \times 10^6~B\overline B$ pairs collected at the KEKB collider by the Belle detector at the $\Upsilon(4S)$ resonance. This marks the first search by the Belle detector for a decay mode involving an anti-neutron. Our analysis found no substantial signal, and we established an $90\%$ credible upper limit on the branching fraction of $6.1\times10^{-6}$.

RobustLoc is proposed to address the limitations of previous camera pose regression models in handling real-world driving scenarios with environmental disturbances.
To overcome idealized conditions where minimal perturbations are assumed, RobustLoc leverages neural differential equations to derive robustness against perturbations.
This approach utilizes a convolutional neural network to extract feature maps from multi-view images and a novel neural differential equation diffusion block module to diffuse information interactively.
A branched pose decoder with multi-layer training is used to estimate vehicle poses, and our experiments show that RobustLoc surpasses the current state-of-the-art models in robust performance across various environments.
Our implementation of RobustLoc is publicly available at: https://github.com/sijieaaa/RobustLoc.

Stable composite particles formed from new non-Abelian gauge forces are potential candidates for dark matter. A key example of this is dark pions that make up the dark matter and determine its abundance through mutual annihilation. The simplest manifestation of this phenomenon is the $Sp(4)_c$ gauge theory with two fermions, which we analyze by examining the meson combinations for both degenerate and non-degenerate fermions. We develop a simplified low-energy model and report on lattice calculations for the properties of pseudoscalar and vector mesons in this theory.

The (001) surface of SnTe topological crystalline insulators hosts significant scientific value and potential for spintronic innovations due to a unique spin configuration. We have investigated the impact of weak optical excitation on the interaction between magnetic impurities on a doped SnTe(001) surface, characterized by peculiar spin-orbit coupling. Our findings reveal a noncollinear, twisted RKKY interaction consisting of XYZ-Heisenberg, symmetric in-plane, and asymmetric DM components. For the majority of cases, the z- and x-components of the XYZ-Heisenberg and DM interactions respectively, exhibit dominant contributions. These complex interactions, particularly those influenced by DM terms, often necessitate doping. To manipulate the interactions, we suggest controlling the SnTe band structure through optical means and corresponding doping modifications, with a notable aspect being the disruption of electron-hole symmetry resulting from DM interaction.

Pre-trained models have achieved notable success in retrieving relevant code snippets from natural language queries. However, existing models primarily focus on embedding code and documentation pairs into a latent space without incorporating external knowledge. In this research, we introduce a framework that leverages a code generation model to augment the code retrieval process. This approach draws inspiration from human search behavior, where an initial answer is sketched before the actual search begins. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by augmenting documentation queries with generated code snippets produced by the code generation model. This innovative approach surpasses existing methods, achieving state-of-the-art results on the CodeSearchNet benchmark.

In $\mathcal{N}=2$ string theory compactifications, we investigate the decay modes of charged black holes with zero temperature. According to the weak gravity conjecture, extremal black holes would typically decay unless they are supersymmetric. We focus on double extremal black holes that maintain constant scalar field values across space-time and explore potential decay paths that favour the formation of BPS and anti-BPS components. We show that tree-level decay channels exist for a wide range of double extremal black holes and, in specific cases, identify stable non-supersymmetric black holes, indicating the possibility of combining (anti-)supersymmetric components to form a non-supersymmetric entity.

In order to meet the escalating performance requirements of neural networks,
accelerator hardware is transitioning to more complex multi-core and chiplet designs.
Current multi-accelerator systems utilize pipelining to increase efficiency by
processing different layers of neural networks across multiple cores for higher throughput.
However, when employing non-batched, layer-by-layer scheduling in latency-sensitive applications,
this approach falls short in maximizing hardware resource utilization for energy-efficient
operation on edge devices.
 
Our work enables the implementation of detailed, layer-by-layer scheduling of
DNNs on multi-core architectures using an open-source modeling framework called Stream.
Stream offers a wide range of scheduling options and supports various hardware architectures,
and it optimizes execution schedules for minimal energy, latency, and/or memory usage
on resource-constrained edge devices. We compare our results to state-of-the-art hardware implementations
and demonstrate close matching of measured efficiencies. Furthermore, our analysis using Stream
reveals that high-level architectural decisions have a significant impact on hardware efficiency
under the fine-grained scheduling paradigm, reducing the energy-delay product by 2.4 to 30 times
in comparison to traditional scheduling at the layer level for single-core and multi-core architectures.

In this paper, we investigate the fundamental characteristics of a recognition network, which is a key component of variational autoencoders and Helmholtz machines, to accurately represent the true posterior distribution of a generative model. Our research focuses on probabilistic graphical modeling and Bayesian networks, where the recognition network embodies a set of conditional independence relationships. We have derived both global and local conditions necessary for the recognition network to model the true posterior distribution, and we found that perfectness of the network structure is a critical factor in achieving this goal.

Fine-tuning pre-trained language models on specific downstream tasks has long been a common approach in natural language processing. However, as these models have grown in size, training them for multiple tasks has become increasingly expensive and resource-intensive. To improve efficiency, recent parameter-efficient tuning techniques have been proposed. Among these methods, a popular approach involves low-rank adaptation techniques, which incorporate learnable truncated SVD modules into the original model. Yet, low-rank decomposition is limited in its representation power. This study addresses this issue by utilizing the Kronecker product instead. We propose KronA, a novel adapter module based on the Kronecker product, designed for the efficient fine-tuning of transformer-based pre-trained language models. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we apply KronA to fine-tune T5 on the GLUE benchmark and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art parameter-efficient tuning methods.

Traditional X-bar charts have been widely utilized to track variations in a process. However, their effectiveness is limited when observations are not normally distributed or contain data contamination, and sample sizes are unequal. To address this, a novel approach is presented for developing robust X-bar control charts that can handle data contamination and unequal sample sizes simultaneously. This method offers the best possible linear unbiased estimation of process parameters. Numerical results show that traditional control charts underperform in the presence of data contamination, but proposed robust control charts outperform them, especially in the presence of outliers.

The J-PARC E36 experiment has recently measured the branching ratio of the structure dependent radiative decay process for $K^{+} \to e^{+} \nu_{e} \gamma$ relative to the decay including internal bremsstrahlung ($K^+\rightarrow e^+ \nu_{e} (\gamma)$), utilizing plastic scintillator/lead sandwich detectors to obtain accurate results. This study accounted for internal bremsstrahlung's influence on the structure dependent radiative decay process, denoted as $K_{e2\gamma(\gamma)}^{\rm SD}$. By combining new data with previously reported results after revising internal bremsstrahlung corrections for the same process, a new branching ratio value was determined to be $1.20\pm0.07$. This result is in line with a recent lattice QCD calculation but larger than expectations based on Chiral Perturbation Theory (ChPT) and a previous value from the KLOE experiment. Furthermore, the study found consistency with the form factor prediction of a gauged nonlocal chiral quark model, but the value still remains larger than ChPT predictions at the order of $O(p^6)$.

This thesis presents a comprehensive investigation into the generation, analysis, and preservation of quantum entanglement within an optical system. The research explores two distinct facets of entanglement: Firstly, we develop and evaluate an experimental approach to creating and characterizing a source of polarization-entangled photons through spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Secondly, we delve into the dynamics of entanglement degradation due to environmental influences and propose novel methods for safeguarding entanglement in lower and higher-dimensional systems against sudden death and decoherence.

Galaxies' gas composition holds valuable information about the processes governing their development, including star birth, energy feedback, gas expulsion and gas ingestion. We have analyzed low redshift galaxy samples to understand the MZR scatter, the contributing factors and their relationship with galaxy mass. Using emission lines to infer cold gas masses and confirming a negative correlation between gas mass and metallicity below a stellar mass threshold, we discovered that halo mass influences gas-poor galaxies' deviation from the MZR. Simulations support the theory that gas ingestion rates vary based on halo mass. At higher stellar masses, AGN activity has a significant effect on metallicity. Our results validate simulations and models, indicating that galaxy metallicity is the result of interactions between gas, outflows, star formation and AGN energy release.

In quantum mechanics, the bra-ket formalism is commonly used for representation-free considerations. However, this formalism has its own set of issues, including ambiguity and complexity. Notably, it relies on a dual-space approach which can be less intuitive than the one-space description that would be more suitable in most scenarios. This work develops a representation-free scheme based on the one-space description, which can also be adapted to fit the dual-space framework as required by certain applications. Before presenting this scheme, the article first discusses the advantages and limitations of the traditional bra-ket formalism. The new scheme eliminates the drawbacks of the bra-ket formalism while still offering all the necessary tools for conducting quantum mechanical representation-free considerations.

Our algorithm estimates the permanent of an arbitrary M x M real matrix A with a given additive error within a polynomial time. We achieve this by considering the permanent of A as the expected value of a product of jointly centered Gaussian random variables, whose covariance matrix is the Gaussian representation of A. The algorithm outputs the empirical average SN of this product after drawing N samples from this multivariate distribution. Specifically, our algorithm takes O(MN) time to run after drawing N samples, with a failure probability that can be expressed as P(|SN - perm(A)| > t) ≤ 3^M / (t^2 N) * α^(2M) for α ≥ the norm of matrix A.

Our investigation into a strong first-order electroweak phase transition in the context of the NMSSM and recent data from the LHC and dark matter experiments has revealed some areas of the model's parameter space where this transition is less likely to occur. Although certain regions that support this phase transition have been ruled out by recent searches, there still exist several other regions that have yet to be constrained by these experiments. Furthermore, we have also examined the potential production of stochastic gravitational waves resulting from this phase transition, both within and outside of established theoretical frameworks.

This paper outlines a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) simulation for the tidal flow within a synthetic port channel based on the dimensions of the Santos - S\~ao Vicente - Bertioga Estuarine System. By merging physical insights with machine learning capabilities, PINNs aim to optimize performance. Our simulation relies on the Navier-Stokes equations with adjusted approximations. Key contributions include the adoption of time-periodic flow assumptions, not typical in traditional simulation methods, and the evaluation of resampling function evaluation points during training, a low-cost approach proven effective, particularly with small data sets. The limitations of Navier-Stokes equation approximations in capturing turbulence and its interaction with PINNs are also explored.

Research has pinpointed noisy and mislabeled training data as the root cause of inaccuracies and untrustworthy output in text generation tasks. To address this issue, it's essential to develop methods for identifying and eliminating low-quality training examples that lead to subpar results. We present a novel framework for pinpointing and removing problematic training data points that result in undesirable outputs, such as inaccuracies in text summaries. Our analysis reveals that conventional methods for tracking errors are not effective in detecting inaccuracies in summaries. By developing an alternative approach that compares problematic outputs to corrected human versions, we can overcome the limitations of existing methods. The proposed approach achieves high accuracy in synthetic tasks and significantly reduces inaccuracies in real-world text generation on the NYT dataset.

Our research into the Zr$_2$Ir compound with a body-centered tetragonal crystal structure has involved first-principles calculations of various physical properties. Our study confirms that Zr$_2$Ir displays both mechanical and dynamic stability, with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects considered. By examining elastic constants, bulk modulus, Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, Debye temperature, and sound velocity, we found Zr$_2$Ir to exhibit ductility. Notably, the influence of SOC leads to a shift from compressibility along the x-axis to the z-axis. Electronic band structure calculations indicate a metallic nature for the compound, with a superconducting critical temperature of 7.50 K and electron-phonon coupling constant of 0.93 in the absence of SOC, increasing to 7.62 K and 0.96 with SOC. Our results suggest that while the compound exhibits strong electron-phonon coupling, SOC has a minor negative effect on the superconducting critical temperature and electron-phonon coupling constant.

In color string models, the transverse momentum distribution (TMD) is derived from the convolution of the Schwinger mechanism with the string tension fluctuations distribution. When assuming a $q$-Gaussian distribution for these fluctuations, the TMD can be represented as a hypergeometric confluent function, effectively capturing characteristic scales at both low and high $p_T$ values. Within this framework, the TMD's hard scale arises from considering a heavy-tailed string tension fluctuations distribution whose width expands as energy or centrality increases. This paper extends the TMD information in the color string percolation model by determining the color suppression factor, now dependent on the $q$-Gaussian parameters. The authors analyzed data on pp and AA collisions at varying energies, multiplicities, and centralities to achieve this, discovering that $q$-Gaussian parameters and effective temperatures increase with center of mass energy in minimum bias pp collisions and with centrality at fixed energy in AA collisions. These findings are visualized in a phase diagram showing the region of $q$-Gaussian parameters suitable for quark-gluon plasma formation.

To study the internal dynamics of nanoscale quantum systems, researchers can utilize thermodynamic probes. Various protocols for directly measuring entropy have been proposed, based on charge transport measurements in single-electron devices. However, existing methods require quasi-equilibrium conditions, which is only a fraction of experimental possibilities. Our study introduces a thermodynamic analysis method grounded in stochastic thermodynamics that can be applied under non-equilibrium conditions and is applicable to a wide range of devices. Using this approach, it's possible to identify the change in entropy between different charge states of the device and the underlying rules governing electron transfers. We've applied this method to a single-molecule device modeled by a two-site Hubbard model.

Multiple Eisenstein series are holomorphic functions defined in the complex upper-half plane, exhibiting characteristics of both classical Eisenstein series and multiple zeta values. Originally formulated by Gangl-Kaneko-Zagier in 2006, their variants and regularizations have since been extensively studied, providing a connection between modular forms and multiple zeta values. This note presents a novel algebraic reinterpretation of stuffle-regularized multiple Eisenstein series, rooted in the Hopf algebra structure of the harmonic algebra, as introduced by Hoffman.

Model-free decision-making processes can be effectively modeled using reinforcement learning, but its exploration-exploitation dilemma persists as an unresolved issue in many scenarios. Our study delves into model-free exploration strategies based on nearby states, suggesting that an agent's early-stage actions can be improved by considering a limited range of neighboring state actions when exploring. To test this hypothesis, we developed two novel algorithms that select exploratory actions based on a survey of nearby states, and discovered that one of these methods, specifically ${\rho}$-explore, significantly outperforms the Double DQN baseline in a discrete environment by 49% in terms of evaluation reward return.

We investigate the remaining gauge freedom in four-dimensional light-cone electromagnetism. The standard boundary conditions of the $lc_2$ formalism, which only account for the two physical degrees of freedom, allow for certain residual gauge transformations. To determine the full set of these residual transformations, we relax the conditions imposed on the fields. Calculating the canonical generators for Poincaré and gauge transformations under these new conditions enables us to distinguish between proper and improper gauge transformations in light-cone electromagnetism. The Newman-Penrose formalism is utilized to identify incoming and outgoing radiation fields, while the structure of light-cone Hamiltonians with quadratic forms in $lc_2$ gauge theories is also addressed.

A method for retrieving semantically aligned sentences that can handle multiple languages is presented, which replaces the need for large batch sizes or complex engineering in contrastive learning. This generative model works efficiently with parallel data from various languages, separating language-specific variations from shared semantic information. A comparison of this method to contrastive and generation-based approaches has been conducted, and it was found that the proposed model outperforms both baselines in several tasks such as semantic similarity, text mining, and cross-lingual question answering. This model is called the Variational Multilingual Source-Separation Transformer, and it achieves state-of-the-art performance in these tasks.

Our research focuses on the distribution of arithmetic properties linked to Alexander
polynomials within specific, infinite families of knots that originate from a fixed
number of braided strings. We establish connections between our findings and number
theory, specifically the distribution of class groups in various number fields, thus
initiating new paths in both arithmetic topology and arithmetic probability.

In ecological systems, processes are typically bounded by physical limitations. One common constraint is the positivity requirement, applicable to factors like time spans, population sizes, and total system reserves. This paper presents a novel approach to embedding dynamic systems within a lognormal state space model, leveraging a method based on matching moments. The proposed method upholds the positivity constraint, enables arbitrary mean evolution and variance structures, and features a closed-form Markov transition density for greater flexibility in fitting techniques. Two existing lognormal state space models are reviewed, highlighting their distinctions from the new method. We evaluate the performance of our approach and existing methods using 180 synthetic datasets, considering model misspecification and precision parameter estimation. Our findings indicate that our models perform well under misspecification and that fixing the observation variance enhances process variance estimation and forecasting accuracy. To assess the robustness of our method, we compare the predictive performance of two lognormal state space models in forecasting Leaf Area Index over a 151-day period using a process-based ecosystem model. The results show that our moment-matching model surpasses its competitor and is more suitable for long-term predictions. This research underscores the significance of incorporating realistic dynamics when modeling complex systems for out-of-sample predictions.

Dementia patients frequently exhibit behaviours that pose a risk to themselves and others, necessitating timely intervention from staff to prevent accidents or fatalities. Existing video monitoring systems in long-term care facilities can identify high-risk behaviours by alerting staff. These events are uncommon compared to everyday occurrences and analyzing raw footage can compromise individuals' privacy. This study presents two innovative methods for privacy-protected video analysis to identify dementia-related risks. We utilized skeleton extraction and semantic masking to anonymize video data. Unlike typical approaches focusing on appearance-based features that compromise individual privacy and are prone to pixel noise, our method uses spatio-temporal autoencoders to identify anomalies from normal activities. We applied these approaches to a real-world study involving dementia care unit patients, utilizing 21 hours of normal activity data for training and 9 hours of data containing normal and high-risk events for testing. The results show equivalent performance, with 0.807 and 0.823 area under the receiver operating characteristic curves for skeleton and segmentation mask-based approaches, respectively. This study is among the first to address the issue of privacy in the context of risk detection in dementia patients.

Building on research related to twisted bilayer graphene, we've developed a lattice-based model for understanding the quantum anomalous Hall effect within a moiré system. Our new model offers a straightforward path to creating a moiré Chern insulator in perfectly aligned twisted models. We analyzed this model in the context of a ribbon shape, revealing a type of chiral edge state that's strongly confined to a particular area, with its confinement increasing as the distance between moiré lattices grows. Additionally, our model allows for the examination of the electronic structure at the boundary between two insulators with opposing properties. The findings from our model are significant, particularly as they pertain to upcoming experiments designed to observe or manipulate the moiré quantum anomalous Hall edge states.

Interest in abstractive summarization has surged lately, fueled by the advancements in pre-trained language models and the availability of substantial datasets. Despite delivering promising results, current models struggle with generating accurate summaries due to factual inconsistencies. Recent attempts to address this limitation have primarily focused on detecting inaccuracies in English language summaries, given its vast resources. In this study, we use factual consistency evaluation models to improve summarization capabilities across languages. Specifically, we examine two methods - data curation and controlled output - that utilize a multilingual NLI model's signals to minimize hallucinations. Our experimental findings on the XLSum dataset in 45 languages reveal significant improvements over established baselines, as evaluated by both machines and humans.

Hydrodynamic turbulence in the form of vertical shear instability (VSI) generates significant vertical mixing and moderate levels of planetary growth in protoplanetary disks, potentially observable in the near future. Using three-dimensional numerical simulations, we investigated VSI behavior within and without embedded planets, then quantified its accretion and mixing effects by comparing total and axisymmetric Reynolds stresses. Our results confirm VSI contributes to planetary accretion, yet an embedded planet can coexist with or suppress VSI activity, depending on disk conditions. Planet-induced features like spiral shocks or vortices can hinder VSI near the planet, but VSI may recover farther away. This suggests that observing VSI signatures is unlikely in disks containing massive non-axisymmetric structures.

The incorporation of feedback loops in biological neural networks, which allows for amplification and damping of output, results in nonlinear behavior that tends towards chaos. Studies in control theory suggest that the complex dynamics associated with strange attractors can be simplified by breaking them down into sets of interconnected cycles and stabilizing the system by focusing control efforts on a central cycle. Drawing on this knowledge, we propose that human memories are encoded by these cyclical patterns, and can be retrieved when relevant sensory or virtual cues trigger feedback mechanisms that bring the chaotic mind into a more focused and coherent state.

Neuromorphic sensors mimic the low-bandwidth, event-driven communication found in biological sensory systems. However, modern sensors produce millions of asynchronous events per second, posing a challenge to conventional computing systems. To mitigate the resulting bottlenecks, there is a pressing need for concurrent and parallel processing techniques. 

To address this issue, we propose AEStream - a framework designed to efficiently handle asynchronous event streams on standard computers. AEStream utilizes coroutines, a type of cooperative multitasking, to simplify the integration with event-driven peripherals and accelerate event processing. Our evaluation of coroutines in concurrent settings demonstrates their superior performance, achieving at least double the throughput compared to traditional threading approaches. Furthermore, we showcase AEStream's effectiveness in a real-time edge detection task on a GPU, achieving 1.3 times faster processing with significantly reduced memory operations - five times fewer to be exact.

We demonstrate that any finite set of quadratic forms derived from general deterministic matrices and the eigenvectors of an $N\times N$ Wigner matrix exhibit joint Gaussian fluctuations, which can be regarded as a random matrix counterpart of the Berry random wave conjecture.

The paper introduces the Epstein Zeta function, a variant of the Eisenstein series, given by $\zeta(s,z)=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2\backslash\{0\}}\frac{(\Im(z))^s}{|mz+n|^{2s}}$. This is motivated by the Lennard-Jones potential, $\mathcal{V}(|\cdot|^2):=4\varepsilon\Big((\frac{\sigma}{|\cdot|})^{12}-(\frac{\sigma}{|\cdot|})^{6} \Big)$, commonly used in physics. Considering this, the paper examines the minimization problem $\min_{z\in\mathbb{H}}\Big(\zeta(6,z)-b\zeta(3,z)\Big)$ with $b=\frac{1}{\sigma^6}$, and provides a comprehensive classification of the minimizers for all real values of $b$. This resolution addresses an open problem in Blanc-Lewin's work and Bétermin's conjecture. Moreover, the paper offers a method for solving the more general problem $\min_{z\in\mathbb{H}}\Big(\zeta(s_1,z)-b\zeta(s_2,z)\Big)$ where $s_1>s_2>1$, which corresponds to a generalized Lennard-Jones potential $\mathcal{V}(|\cdot|^2):=4\varepsilon\Big((\frac{\sigma}{|\cdot|})^{2s_1}-(\frac{\sigma}{|\cdot|})^{2s_2} \Big)$ with $s_1>s_2>1$.

Helium-4's liquid state is uniquely devoid of magnetic flaws, making it an ideal surface for maintaining electrons with prolonged spin stability. Such long-lived spin states can be used as the basis for qubits. We are investigating the spin dynamics of electrons confined within quantum dots on a helium surface, focusing on the electrostatic localization. Effective gate operations within this system require the incorporation of spin-orbit coupling, which can be generated through the use of a nonuniform magnetic field created by an electric current. This field can be precisely controlled and turned on or off, allowing for a substantial increase in the electrostatic dipole moment and the rapid coupling of adjacent dot spins. Crucially, understanding the rate at which spin states decay due to spin-orbit coupling is essential. Our study identifies the primary cause of this decay and demonstrates that it is slow enough to enable the execution of high-fidelity single- and two-qubit gate operations.

The increasing interest in experimental quantum technology has led to a growing focus on quantum control due to the creation of controllable artificial quantum systems. Since dealing with quantum-mechanical systems analytically can be challenging, heuristic strategies and numerical algorithms are adopted to find suitable control protocols. Deep learning, particularly deep reinforcement learning (RL), holds promise as a universal solution for these control problems. Although deep RL has been successfully applied to some quantum control issues, existing RL algorithms are often plagued by instability and a lack of reproducibility, and they require extensive fine-tuning and computational resources. To address these problems, this dissertation investigates the non-convergence issue in Q-learning and identifies the weaknesses in existing convergent approaches. As a result, a new convergent Q-learning algorithm, known as the convergent deep Q network (C-DQN), is developed to replace the conventional deep Q network (DQN) algorithm. The convergence of C-DQN is proven, and its application to the Atari 2600 benchmark demonstrates its effectiveness when DQN fails. Additionally, C-DQN is used to tackle measurement-feedback cooling problems in quantum systems, showcasing its stability and superior performance when compared to DQN. These results suggest that C-DQN can be a more reliable choice for complex control problems.

The Lattice Boltzmann method can be improved with a free energy model to handle complex multiphase systems. Currently, there is a shortage of models capable of accurately simulating multi-component, partially miscible fluids, and existing models are not compatible with various thermodynamic equations of state. This paper introduces a new free energy Lattice Boltzmann model where the key driving factor is the species fugacity, a critical property that links partial pressures and chemical potential. With this model, it's possible to run simulations of partially miscible fluids and make them compatible with any desired thermodynamic equation of state. The new method is then tested on various scenarios involving two and three-component mixtures under different temperature and pressure conditions, demonstrating its ability to predict phase properties and compositions accurately according to thermodynamic principles. Moreover, the model shows its potential to provide reliable results in dynamic systems.

Our research aims to build upon previous studies that estimated the uncertainty linked to the interactions between nucleons and the target nucleus. This study goes beyond that by also considering the properties of the mean field that influences the overlap function of the final bound state, thereby providing a comprehensive assessment of the parametric uncertainty affecting transfer observables. The method employed involves using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations to generate posterior distributions of the parameters. These simulations utilize elastic-scattering cross sections to restrict the parameters of the optical potential and the asymptotic normalization coefficient of the final state to constrain the bound state interaction. The obtained posteriors are then propagated to the transfer angular distributions to yield confidence intervals for this observable. In our analysis, we examined (d,p) reactions on 14C, 16O, and 48Ca at various energies ranging from 10 to 24 MeV. The results show a significant reduction in uncertainty by incorporating the asymptotic normalization coefficient as a constraint, particularly for reactions that are highly sensitive to ambiguities in the mean field. We found that constraining the bound state interaction is equally crucial to restricting the optical potential parameters for such reactions. However, the case of 14C deviates from this pattern due to its propensity to form a halo state, making the observable less susceptible to the nuclear interior. Our findings demonstrate that when minimal constraints are applied to the nucleon-target interaction, the 68% confidence interval uncertainties on differential cross sections are excessively large, ranging from 140 to 185%. Nevertheless, if elastic-scattering data and the asymptotic normalization coefficient are utilized in the analysis, with a 10% (5%) error margin, the uncertainty is significantly reduced to approximately 30% (15%).

The Atom portal, accessible at udel.edu/atom, serves the scientific community by offering an easily accessible, high-quality database of atomic and ionic properties, including energy levels, transition characteristics, decay rates, and physical constants. This comprehensive dataset is computed using a state-of-the-art, high-precision linearized coupled-cluster method, complemented by high-precision experimental values where feasible. All calculated values are accompanied by estimated uncertainty ranges. Whenever possible, experimental findings are supplemented with relevant references. The paper offers a comprehensive overview of the portal's architecture, highlighting its underlying design principles and software engineering methodologies.

Recent studies have demonstrated the exceptional capabilities of transformer-based language models in various natural language processing tasks. This paper focuses on the transformer models BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet, both in their smaller and larger versions, to assess their faithfulness in accurately representing the semantic content of written texts. A novel notion of semantic faithfulness was introduced, which emphasizes that a model's responses to questions should be grounded in the underlying semantic meaning of the text. To test this notion, the models' behavior was examined when answering questions about a story after two innovative manipulations were performed - the removal of certain elements (deletion intervention) and the reversal of statements (negation intervention). Despite achieving high performance in standard question-answering tasks, transformer models showed significant failures in semantic faithfulness when these manipulations were applied (approximately 50% for deletion and a 20% decrease in accuracy for negation). A novel training regime was proposed to mitigate the adverse effects of deletion intervention, resulting in a substantial improvement (from approximately 50% to 6%). An analysis of the models' inner workings revealed the effectiveness of this training approach. However, it failed to address other forms of semantic unfaithfulness, such as the models' inability to handle negation intervention and to identify the relationships between subjects, actions, and objects in texts. Additionally, the InstructGPT model was tested using prompts to evaluate its capacity to deal with the two interventions and to recognize the predicate-argument structure of texts. While InstructGPT achieved high performance in identifying predicate-argument structures, it struggled to respond adequately to the deletion and negation interventions.

To define a canonical ensemble for a gravitational causal diamond, we first create a man-made York boundary within the diamond that has a fixed induced metric and temperature, then use a saddle point approximation to compute the partition function. For Einstein gravity without a cosmological constant, no exact saddle exists with a horizon; however, in the high-temperature limit, an approximate saddle emerges within the Euclidean diamond, where its horizon approaches the artificial boundary. This high-temperature partition function provides a statistical interpretation of a prior entropy calculation, where the entropy of causal diamonds was recovered from an on-shell Euclidean action boundary term by Banks, Draper, and Farkas. Conversely, when a positive cosmological constant is present, or in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity with or without a cosmological constant, an exact saddle with a finite boundary temperature exists, and the causal diamond is determined by this saddle rather than being predetermined.

A novel approach to quantizing continuous and discrete time Birth and Death processes has been proposed. This procedure transforms the matrix representing the BD equation by relating it to the square root of its stationary distribution. Consequently, the resulting quantum and classical systems exhibit identical eigenvalues and one-to-one correspondence between their eigenvectors. Specifically, if the birth and death rates are chosen according to certain conditions derived from the Askey scheme of orthogonal polynomials, the quantum system becomes solvable. In such cases, the eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be explicitly determined, with many examples displaying periodic behavior due to their integer-valued eigenvalues. This framework bears strong resemblance to one-dimensional exactly solvable quantum mechanical systems, offering adjustable parameters that could be beneficial for simulation purposes.

A frequency rectangle is an m by n matrix where each symbol from a set of q elements appears n/q times in each row and m/q times in each column. Two such frequency rectangles are considered orthogonal if when superimposed, every possible ordered pair of symbols occurs the same number of times. A collection of k frequency rectangles where every pair is orthogonal is called a set of mutually orthogonal frequency rectangles. We prove a set of k mutually orthogonal frequency rectangles of type (2,2n;2) is equivalent to an orthogonal array of type OA(2n,k,2,2). Furthermore, we show that an OA(mn,k,2,2) implies the existence of a k--MOFR(2m,2n;2). By assuming the existence of a Hadamard matrix of order 4a, we construct a (4a-2)--MOFR(4,2a;2). A k--MOFR(m,n;q) is considered t-orthogonal if each subset of t, when superimposed, contains each of the q^t possible ordered t-tuples the same number of times. We explain how to obtain a set of t-orthogonal k--MOFR(q^M, q^N, q) from a set of t-independent vectors in (F_q)^(M+N). Additionally, we discuss upper and lower bounds on the set of t-independent vectors and provide a table of binary vectors of length N ≤ 16. A frequency rectangle of type FR(n,n;q) is called a frequency square and a collection of k mutually orthogonal frequency squares is denoted by k--MOFS(n;q). For a given odd prime p, we show there exists a set of (p-1) binary MOFS(2p) thus improving the lower bounds for p ≥ 19 established in (Britz et al. 2020).

A precise mathematical equation governing the movement of defect lines in liquid crystals, in relation to the nematic material's molecular alignment, is established. This mathematical model is based on a unique property of the nematic material's molecular order parameter, which remains constant at the defect site despite the presence of defects. Following earlier research, the location of the defect is identified as the point at which the material's order parameter transitions from one-dimensional to two-dimensional alignment, or where the molecular alignment changes direction. By relating the speed of the defect line to the changes in the nematic material's molecular alignment, an exact expression for the defect's motion is formulated. This expression is derived from a theoretical model describing the evolution of the nematic material. A simplified approximation of the nematic material's molecular alignment is used to obtain analytical solutions for specific scenarios, including interactions and motion between defects, their annihilation, and their response to external influences. The resulting solutions are consistent with numerical simulations that account for the nematic material's anisotropic elasticity and three-dimensional structure.

A novel coinless quantisation method is introduced for general reversible Markov chains defined on graphs. The quantum Hamiltonian is derived by transforming the fundamental transition matrix into a form involving the square root of the reversible distribution's eigenvalue. Solutions to the eigenvalue problem of this quantum Hamiltonian describe the evolution of both classical and quantum Markov chains. Utilizing exactly solvable Markov chains based on Askey scheme hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials, specifically those developed by Odake-Sasaki, allows for an in-depth examination of the quantum-classical dichotomy in Markov chains. To exemplify this, explicit examples related to the Krawtchouk, Hahn, q-Hahn, Charlier, and Meixner distributions are employed to demonstrate the feasibility of this method.

We propose an analogy with the black hole information paradox resolution, using it as a model to theorize the state of consciousness. This involves the Page curve and Page time, which we draw from to identify the key parameter governing consciousness. Crucial to our theory are the interconnectedness between brain state and temporal patterns of neuronal firing, as well as the non-independent nature of brain network structures.

A fundamental limit has been identified regarding the distillation of entanglement from mixed quantum states via local operations. Specifically, it's been proven that a $2\otimes 2$ or $2\otimes 3$ system can't be purified by separable or local operations, but a $3\otimes 3$ system can be purified by separable operations, though not by local ones. Notably, a breakthrough was made in proving that a $2\otimes 4$ system can be distilled by local operations, and the findings have been generalized to purify a pure entangled state of Schmidt rank $d$ from a $m\otimes n$ mixed state by separable operations, under the condition that $m+n \geqslant 3d$. Additionally, the work has provided new insights into the capabilities of separable operations in tripartite systems, where a target $d$-level GHZ-type state can be distilled, and it's been demonstrated that separable operations are strictly more powerful than local operations in these cases.

Research has revealed that generated text from large language models often
displays a range of biased views that mirror societal prejudices towards
certain demographics. As a result, a significant effort has been made to study
and evaluate these effects, with the ultimate goal of developing standards to
measure the effectiveness of techniques that reduce stereotypical associations.
However, a recent study pointed out that the existing benchmarks lack a
sufficiently rigorous methodology, which in turn limits the validity of their
evaluation metrics. In this paper, we expand on these concerns, highlighting
that current techniques and benchmarks aimed at detecting biases in language
models are often inaccurate and plagued by experimental errors, which severely
hinders our understanding of these models. Consequently, we propose a new
methodology for measuring and quantifying biases in language models in a more
reliable manner. We then apply this framework to analyze the occupational
gender bias of GPT-3 and present techniques for mitigating these biases without
requiring fine-tuning of the model.

Traditional software development frameworks have been well-established, 
but the creation of AI-based systems presents novel difficulties due to their 
lack of transparent inner workings. Existing studies have mainly concentrated 
on employing AI to oversee requirements engineering, with limited investigation 
into requirements engineering for AI (RE4AI). This research examines current 
methods for formulating AI system requirements, recognizes existing frameworks, 
methodologies, tools, and modeling techniques, and identifies current 
shortcomings and constraints. A systematic mapping study was conducted to 
determine papers on present RE4AI methodologies. Forty-three primary studies 
were found and analyzed, revealing existing methodologies, models, tools, and 
techniques used to define and model AI system requirements in real-world
